glossary.Altered bowel habit: A change in how often or how loose or hard stools are.
glossary.Diarrhoea: Passing loose or watery stools more often than usual.
glossary.Cramps: Painful squeezing spasms of the gut muscle.
glossary.Mucus: Slimy fluid made by the bowel lining, sometimes seen in the stool in IBS.
glossary.Diffuse: Spread over a wide area rather than in one spot.
glossary.Tenderness: Pain when the area is pressed on examination.
glossary.Anxiety: Persistent worry or fear, which can worsen IBS symptoms.
glossary.Depression: Persistent low mood and loss of interest, common alongside IBS.
glossary.Systemic illness: Illness affecting the whole body, such as fever or weight loss.
glossary.Obstruction: Blockage of the bowel, giving vomiting, distension and absolute constipation.
glossary.Differentials: Other conditions that could explain the same symptoms.
glossary.Diagnosis of exclusion: A diagnosis made once other possible causes have been ruled out.
glossary.Malabsorption: Poor absorption of nutrients from the gut, as in coeliac disease.
glossary.Thyroid: Neck gland whose overactivity causes diarrhoea and underactivity causes constipation.
glossary.Lifestyle: Changes to daily habits such as meals, fluids, sleep and exercise.
glossary.Caffeine: Stimulant in coffee and tea that speeds up the gut.
glossary.Soluble fibre: Fibre that dissolves in water to form a gel, softening stool, e.g. ispaghula and oats.
glossary.Bulking agent: A fibre laxative that adds bulk and water to stool.
glossary.Motility: Movement of contents along the gut by muscle contractions.
glossary.Distension: Stretching or swelling of the bowel or abdomen.
glossary.Pain threshold: The level of stimulus at which a sensation is first felt as pain.
glossary.Gastroenteritis: Infection of the stomach and bowel causing vomiting and diarrhoea.
glossary.Mucosal inflammation: Inflammation of the inner lining of the bowel.
glossary.Fermentable carbohydrates: Sugars and fibres that gut bacteria break down, producing gas.
glossary.Smooth muscle: Involuntary muscle in the gut wall that produces peristalsis.
glossary.Antidepressant: A drug used to treat depression; in IBS low doses are used for pain.
glossary.Neutrophil: A white blood cell that floods inflamed tissue.
glossary.Visceral pain: Dull, poorly localised pain from internal organs.
glossary.Mebeverine hydrochloride: Antispasmodic that relaxes gut smooth muscle; first-line for IBS pain and cramps.
glossary.Psychological stress: Mental strain that can trigger or worsen IBS via the gut-brain axis.
glossary.Quality of life: A person's overall wellbeing and ability to enjoy daily life.
